- When sentiment is neutral or absent, model tends to overestimate prices in early periods and underestimates in late periods — adjust forecast mid-horizon downward if no sentiment signal.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the immediate next period — apply a 1–2 day lag correction or reduce peak forecast by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., -1.00), model consistently underestimates true price — increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizons — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- In low-sentiment periods, model exhibits “early overreaction” — forecast first 5–7 days too high, then corrects — apply a 3–5 day smoothing filter or dampen initial peaks.
- If true outcome shows strong upward trend after model’s peak, model often fails to capture momentum — add 1–2% lagged momentum adjustment to forecast tail.
